messages:
elena: Thanks everyone — thread for follow-ups from today's all-hands. Drop questions about strategy, market positioning, and competitor calls here. I'll respond through the day.

rachel: Quick ask from hiring: are we still prioritizing inference infra hires this quarter or shifting to product growth roles?
jia: Also want more color on our 'same API everywhere' claim can we give a simple customer-facing example?
anil: Curious on competitive posture: do we call out hyperscalers directly in enablement, or keep messaging product-first?
elena: Short answers: hiring mix stays infra-heavy for Q2 (approx 60% infra/serving, 40% product/growth).
elena: For customers: "One SDK, one set of paths switch from hosted to private without code changes." Example: change endpoint to private and set policy flag; app keeps calling same client.
marco: Sales question: any concrete metrics we should lead with vs competitors? e.g., % cost savings, latency p95 numbers? reps want soundbites.
sara: and for product folks: what are the top 3 roadmap items for next release cycle that we should defend?
elena: Metrics for GTM: lead with predictable p95 latency and cost-per-token reduction via caching/batching. We'll publish a one-pager with p50/p95 numbers across common configs.
elena: Top roadmap priorities: 1) Canary rollouts + automatic rollback, 2) KV/prefix caching improvements, 3) Dedicated autoscaling policies.
jia: follow-up: on canary rollouts are we supporting traffic-based canary or weight-based? can we have sticky user routing?
anil: on competitor tone: recommend product-first; call out differences concretely (e.g., private deploy, rollout controls) but avoid naming hyperscalers in formal docs. Enablement can include direct comparisons.
marco: pricing guidance: are we setting public ranges for Dedicated or only quoting per-deal? reps need ranges to qualify earlier.
elena: We'll publish ranges for typical Dedicated configs (small/medium/large) but keep final pricing per-deal. That should help qualification.
sara: Will there be an updated battlecard for SI partners? they asked for compliance + deployment checklist.
elena: Yes SI battlecard + compliance checklist dropping next Friday.
ops-bot: Recording + slides uploaded: https://redwood/ah/1840001111 (auto-upload)
rachel: Marketing: what's our core positioning line for the next quarter? we used a few variants today.
elena: Current short tag: "Redwood Inference Serve predictably. Ship faster. Pay less." We want it short and benefit-driven.
jia: any specific competitor features we should highlight to engineering customers? i.e., kernel optimizations, kv caching, or orchestration?
elena: Engineers: highlight runtime kernel selection + KV cache and pinned model variants for rollouts. That's a practical differentiation.
marco: one more from sales ops: target for new logos from Dedicated/Private this year? a band is fine.
elena: Goal: 25	-	28% of new logo ACV from Dedicated/Private this fiscal. Not public-facing but shared internally.
sara: product question: will public hosted SLOs change? some customers asked for stricter p95 SLAs.
elena: Hosted SLAs will remain the same for now; we'll document clear upgrade paths to Dedicated for stricter SLOs.
anil: Any plan to open-source performance benchmarks or keep them internal?
elena: We'll publish curated benchmark summaries (anonymized configs) for developer trust but keep detailed internal lab runs private.
jia: thanks this helps for docs work.
marco: i'll coordinate with sales enablement to get the ranges into the CRM.
ops-bot: Action created: link to canary roadmap doc will be posted here by EOD.
elena: Thanks team, i'll post the roadmap link + the GTM one-pager later today. Keep questions coming. :raised_hands:
